Compliance reporting - internal communication practice

Original wording: Put this out on Friday.

documents.name: community-reference-rooms
documents.title: Rooms and staff reservations
documents.text:
Rooms and staff reservations

Edda Velswick · 2026-06-05

Use the full site and room name in an invitation. The Regional office small meeting room seats four; the Regional office meeting room seats ten. Pine and River each have a plant staff room and a depot briefing room with eight seats. These are staff discussion spaces, not permission to enter an operational area.

Ask Records and scheduling for a reservation with a start and end time. Include telephone participation where it helps. Count the people physically present before adding another chair. A room hold still reserves capacity even if some invitees have not answered.

When a meeting is cancelled, release the reservation and tell the invitees. Return chairs and display equipment to their usual place. Shared availability shows Reserved and the times. Private subjects and the people attending belong only in the invitation.

documents.name: community-reference-appointments
documents.title: Private staff appointments
documents.text:
Private staff appointments

Flora Odrin · 2026-06-05

Contact the named People Services colleague or your manager to arrange a private staff conversation. Give the times that fit your work and say whether a telephone or written exchange would be easier. The booking request does not need a personal explanation on a shared calendar.

Agree cover before leaving a desk or duty. The covering colleague needs the released time and what remains available; they do not need the private invitation or its attachment. If the appointment moves, update the invitees and send a separate cover-time notice.

A retained note should describe the decision, the outstanding question and who will act next. Keep it with the named employee, manager and any People Services colleague actually involved. A conversation about development does not itself change a job, pay or reporting line.

documents.name: community-reference-learning
documents.title: Arranging an internal learning session
documents.text:
Arranging an internal learning session

Gabriel Wellard · 2026-06-05

Start with the question the learner wants to answer. Identify a colleague who can help and use a blank or appropriately shared example. Allow preparation time as well as the session itself; someone explaining familiar work may still need time to choose a useful example.

The manager should agree a time that fits duty and any necessary cover. A local or telephone session can avoid an unnecessary office journey. Keep the useful written material available to other shifts without exposing a learner's private record.

After the session, record the example tried and anything still to practise. Attendance, an accepted invitation and a successful assessment are different things. Internal communication practice does not grant operating authority, access permissions or a professional qualification. A purchased course also needs its own approved arrangement.

documents.name: community-reference-notices
documents.title: Publishing a staff notice
documents.text:
Publishing a staff notice

Dario Torren · 2026-06-05

Put the practical information first: what the reader needs to know, the full date, the place and a contact for questions. Give the notice an owner and a review or expiry date. Avoid next Thursday on a retained copy unless the full date appears beside it.

Choose the audience before circulating the text. A depot arrangement may need only that depot; a staff reference can serve the whole company. A private personnel matter belongs with its named readers, not in a notice disguised as a general reminder.

For paper copies, record which boards or folders received the current version. Remove an expired sheet from the sleeve rather than hiding it behind the new one. Keep the earlier record where history is retained; the current board should make the current invitation easy to identify.

documents.name: community-reference-contributions
documents.title: Contributing a memory or caption
documents.text:
Contributing a memory or caption

Della Delmont · 2026-06-05

A contribution can be a sentence. Tell the editor whether you witnessed the event or learned about it later, and whether you want your name displayed. Nobody needs a long service history to describe arriving, learning a local name or finding a useful colleague.

The editor will send the actual proposed wording and intended audience for your approval. A private conversation or a possible draft is not publication permission. You can ask for a correction, more time or withdrawal before publication. A layout deadline does not override that choice.

Do not include another person's private story without their agreement. Photographs need the contributor's permission for the intended display. A caption review does not mean an image has been supplied, and a staff display does not automatically approve public reuse.

documents.name: community-reference-formats
documents.title: Requesting a useful format
documents.text:
Requesting a useful format

Dev Mavell · 2026-06-05

Tell Records and scheduling which staff page you need and what makes it difficult to use. You can ask for larger print, a text version, a simpler table or a dated paper copy at your site. Send the request privately if it includes personal information.

Try the revised copy before treating the request as finished. A larger version of a crowded table may remain crowded. Row labels, shorter headings and a repeated date on the second page can help more than increasing every line of text.

When sharing a paper copy, keep its title, date and contact for questions. Do not add a private reason for the requested format to the notice. Operational and customer records retain their own authorized versions; this service concerns staff information.

documents.name: community-reference-shift-participation
documents.title: Staff information across shifts
documents.text:
Staff information across shifts

Nina Rivelin · 2026-06-05

An office-hours invitation will not fit every shift. Organizers should ask which times and local arrangements are workable before treating a group list as an attendance list. Written questions and local sessions are useful alternatives when the information does not require everybody in one room.

A released operator or field colleague needs an agreed time and named cover. Existing handovers, visits and practical training remain commitments. Do not leave duty uncovered because a calendar application accepted an invitation. Tell the organizer when the proposed time conflicts.

Keep the useful staff explanation available to other crews. Optional social participation is separate from necessary work information. Nobody should need to attend an unpaid social gathering or travel to the main office to find the current staff form or contact.

documents.name: community-reference-calendar
documents.title: Invitations and responses
documents.text:
Invitations and responses

Edda Velswick · 2026-06-05

An invitation states the purpose, start, end and location. If attendance is optional, say so plainly. Give a way to decline or ask for another arrangement. A tentative hold is useful while availability is checked, but it is not a confirmed event.

Keep accepted, declined, tentative and unanswered responses distinct. An unanswered person has not agreed simply because their team lead is attending. If the event is cancelled, retain the cancellation and release any room or resource reservation. A replacement gets its own invitation referring to the earlier one.

After a completed event, record actual attendance when a work record needs it. Do not use calendar acceptance as attendance evidence. Formal minutes are useful for decisions, actions or learning outcomes; a short social break need not acquire an artificial agenda or action list.

documents.name: community-reference-contacts
documents.title: Finding the current owner
documents.text:
Finding the current owner

Dario Torren · 2026-06-05

The staff directory contains current teams, roles and work contacts. Start there when an older handout names somebody whose responsibilities have changed. A former role can explain a historical record without making that person the current owner of every request.

When asking for a correction, include the page title, date and the confusing pointer. Records and scheduling will check the contact with the responsible team before replacing the staff copy. Do not forward a private case or personnel record merely to discover where it belongs.

The directory identifies colleagues; it does not grant access to their documents or applications. Ask for the particular information through the normal authorized route. Shared mailboxes, rooms and external contractors remain distinct from employees, even when their names appear in ordinary working correspondence.

documents.name: community-reference-community
documents.title: Preparing a community explanation
documents.text:
Preparing a community explanation

Rosa Nerivet · 2026-09-11

Begin with the visitor's question. The agreed preparation outline asks what happens before water reaches our tap, then introduces source water, treatment, distribution and customer service. Leave time to hear what the visitor actually wants explained.

The relay comparison helps describe different responsibilities contributing to one service. Make clear that the work continues throughout the day; one department does not permanently finish when another takes over. The separate Pine and River services joined in 2009, but that history need not be the opening for every audience.

The September 10 rehearsal is preparation. The community group's public session date remains unsettled. Do not announce a time or use preparation as evidence of an operational qualification. Individual billing or meter questions belong with customer service through the appropriate private route.

documents.name: community-reference-photos
documents.title: Ordinary light and the staff display
documents.text:
Ordinary light and the staff display

Della Delmont · 2026-09-15

Ordinary light is a voluntary staff photography activity using pictures taken on personal time. Phone pictures are welcome. A colleague can contribute to the display without entering the competition; participation in either part is optional.

Entries closed September 14 and results were circulated September 15. Kaisa Kelswick's kitchen-window photograph placed first and Theo Marrivel's early-morning footpath placed second. Accepted entries from Mina Selverin and Owen Vardell are included in the display arrangements. Ask before changing a contributor's caption or using their picture for another audience.

The October staff walk is a separate plan whose date and route remain unsettled. A photograph contribution does not book a place on it. The retained results and caption correspondence describe the activity; they do not include image files or approve public reuse.

documents.name: community-reference-history
documents.title: Reading the company history
documents.text:
Reading the company history

Luc Venn-Morel · 2026-09-11

Pine and River operated separate water services before joining in 2009. Shared planning, purchasing and management developed while local depots continued their work. Colleagues who joined later may know the regional organization much better than either predecessor.

The staged distribution renewal of 2014 to 2017 and treatment refurbishment of 2021 to 2023 are parts of that history. Project records describe scope, dates and results. Staff recollections can describe the work of fitting a stage around other duties, without claiming to speak for every contributor.

For induction, a small discussion can be more useful than a speech. Agree the people, preparation time and cover before promising a visit. A new colleague does not need to have worked on an older project to take pride in the service now.

documents.name: community-reference-optional
documents.title: Optional staff activities
documents.text:
Optional staff activities

Flora Odrin · 2026-06-05

A staff activity invitation should make clear whether participation is optional. A decline needs no private explanation. Unanswered invitations stay unanswered; do not ask another colleague to account for someone's absence. People can enjoy one gathering and skip the next.

Check working hours, duty cover and travel before suggesting a time. Small groups at different sites may work better than one main-office occasion. If useful staff information is shared, provide it separately so a social invitation does not become a condition of learning something necessary.

Contribution to a display, attendance at a walk and volunteering for outreach are separate choices. A date still under discussion is not a booking. Keep private friendships and weekend arrangements with their participants rather than presenting them as company programmes.

documents.name: community-reference-handover
documents.title: A useful staff handover note
documents.text:
A useful staff handover note

Eira Dravik · 2026-06-05

Write the part the next person needs: what changed, when it changed, what remains open and who holds the next action. Name the copy or notice rather than saying the latest one. A full date survives leave and a change of shift better than yesterday.

Separate an observed outcome from a proposed next step. A booked appointment is not a completed conversation, and a sent message does not prove that its recipient has accepted the request. Keep the outstanding question visible instead of ending every note with completed.

Use the audience appropriate to the subject. A cover handover needs the duty and time, not the reason for a private staff appointment. Operational handovers retain their own approved records; these examples concern ordinary staff arrangements.

documents.name: community-reference-display
documents.title: Display resources
documents.text:
Display resources

Elias Narsen · 2026-06-05

Records and scheduling keeps the staff display board and portable reading stand available by reservation. Give the location, start, end and return arrangement. Check the room separately: having a display resource does not reserve a room or increase its capacity.

Use the shared availability list to avoid an overlapping reservation. It shows only the resource and the reserved time. The organizer keeps the purpose and any contributor details with the named participants. A cancelled arrangement releases both the room and the resource.

Before putting material on the board, check the intended audience and publication permission. Leave captions readable without blocking access to the room. Return the board or stand to the agreed location after use; if the arrangement changes, tell the next borrower rather than moving it silently.

documents.name: community-reference-billing-pointer
documents.title: Finding the billing-period explanation
documents.text:
Finding the billing-period explanation

Rosa Nerivet · 2026-09-15

The accepted staff explanation is titled Which period does my water bill cover? and is dated September 15, 2026. It starts with the interval identified on the bill, then distinguishes that interval from the date the bill was issued.

The bill also identifies the readings used for metered consumption and whether they are actual or estimated. Customer service can explain unclear entries on the individual account. A person asking a question need not reconstruct the company's internal process first.

Use the accepted explanation rather than writing a competing version from this pointer. A question about a bill does not itself book a meter visit, change a tariff or settle a balance. Keep individual account details in the authorized customer-service records; general staff reference pages should not contain them.

documents.name: community-outreach-handout
documents.title: Before water reaches our tap - handout
documents.text:
# Before water reaches our tap

What happens before water reaches our tap?

ARWC looks after a connected service. People obtain source water, treat it,
keep the distribution system working and help customers understand the service
they receive. The work continues throughout the day. Different responsibilities
contribute to the same result; one group does not permanently finish when
another takes over.

Think of arranging an ordinary meter visit. A customer-service colleague helps
agree the appointment, field colleagues do the practical work, and the account
records the result. The people doing those jobs need one another's information.

What would you like to ask about that journey?

For a question about your own bill or meter appointment, contact customer
service privately. Please do not put your account details on a shared question
sheet. Asking a general question here does not book a visit.

No public invitation has been issued. Keep the draft arrangements with the
preparers until the group and staff agree a workable date.

documents.name: op-books-guide
documents.title: Operations books: local reading guide
documents.text:
# Operations books: August 3–September 13, 2026

These books retain the plant round handovers and selected morning distribution routes for six weeks. Overnight plant turns finish on September 14. They are not a complete attendance or payroll record. The books include filter-run time, differential-head observations and completed routine wash entries. Other process readings remain in the operating log; field identity visits do not create billing readings.

Plant turns run 06:00–14:00, 14:00–22:00 and 22:00–06:00. Four crews rotate two turns of each kind, followed by two rest days. The named lead checks the round entries before handover. Amara Fennard joins accompanied River rounds after her August 26 induction; independent local sign-off is pending. Mina's September 9 night turn is covered by the remaining crew so daytime preparation and the September 10 outreach rehearsal stay clear.

Distribution duty runs 07:00–15:00 on weekdays. Twenty people form ten pairs in each district; two remain on depot relief. The morning visit is only part of the duty. Briefing, outward travel, returns, meal breaks, stores work and afternoon practice fit around it. Vans and kits are held 08:00–12:30. The lead drives. Owen's lead is an experienced distribution technician and retains the operational decision.

Field Desk appointments record an agreed service-desk window; the organizer manages the booking and does not attend. A no-access return does not verify a meter. These visits inspect identity and approach only: no billable reading, meter exchange, supply interruption, valve operation or confined-space entry. Account references are included to route the return correctly. Names, contact details, preferences and balances remain with Customer Service.

Sample entries stop at receipt of the sealed package. Use the sample reference for laboratory work; the field return is not a water-quality result. A maintenance request acknowledges an observed condition. Receipt by Maintenance does not mean a repair has been scheduled or completed. Small marking and housekeeping work completed by the field pair is described in the visit return.

Stock is counted in each, with physical opening, issue, return and closing quantities. A returned empty sleeve is waste, not usable stock. Training records describe observed supervised practice, not qualifications. Keep later decisions on a dated new record rather than rewriting an earlier handover.

documents.title: Selected-books accounting basis
documents.text:
# Selected-books accounting basis

Effective June 1, 2026. Finance lead: Emre Edran. Approved by Elin Verrin.

These management control accounts cover the purchasing register and the customer water-account book. They are not statutory accounts, a complete balance sheet, an operating profit statement or a bank confirmation. Payroll, depreciation, other company banking and general-ledger classification are outside this close. USD is the reporting currency; the source invoices carry zero sales tax.

The May 31 collection-account float is USD 500,000.00: Pine USD 275,000.00 and River USD 225,000.00. It is a designated opening management balance carried from earlier activity; no current-period income, borrowing or transfer is invented to explain it. The selected customer invoice book has no invoice before June 1. Earlier supplier acquisitions and settlements are carried separately from their dated records.

An invoice increases the customer control; a signed credit reduces it. Count each accepted receipt once, whether it has one or several allocations. Bill display copies are not new invoices. Billed charges can concern earlier consumption, so billing is not current-month earned revenue. The July 1 account projection is not used as a universal transaction date; later Talvern invoices and settlements retain their June/July dates.

Supplier matches enter the acquisitions control and payables. Acquisitions remain inventory or operating expense pending general-ledger classification. Payment reduces cash and payables. A receipt without a matched invoice is shown as GRNI, separately from payables; an unreceived order is a commitment, not a receipt or expense. These memorandum balances are not added to acquisitions a second time.

PINE-OPS and RIVER-OPS remain local. REGIONAL-SHARED uses the accepted 55% Pine / 45% River transaction allocations, including the River cent residual. This 2026 shared-support method is not the ownership ratio and is not automatically applied to a new capital project. Historical capital amounts are prior-period accepted costs, not current payments. Internal control cash is reconciled to receipts and supplier settlements, not claimed reconciled to an external bank statement.

# 2026-06-30 customer reconciliation

Opening receivables USD 0.00; issued invoices USD 517.50; signed adjustments USD 0.00; receipts USD 517.50; closing receivables USD 0.00.

Amara's customer book remains authoritative at invoice level. Combine its original receipts with accepted later retail payments, once each. Allocation rows explain application, not additional cash. Credits retain their negative sign. Talvern's separate dated seasonal settlements are included only when due to this cutoff. An account arrangement is a promise, not a receipt.

This is the net control for the selected accounts, not an aged-debt statement or proof that every customer owes money. A credit balance stays a credit. Customer names, premises, contacts and individual balances are excluded from the board and public summaries.

# 2026-06-30 receipts and settlement bridge

Management collection-account opening USD 500,000.00; customer receipts USD 517.50; supplier settlements USD 44,199.40; closing USD 456,318.10.

The opening float is a carried balance, not new income. No closing transfer is used as a plug. The source of this bridge is the receipt and settled-payment registers; there is no external bank statement in this pack. Felix checked that the payment allocation register was not added to the receipt register and that invoices marked payable did not enter cash outflow.

The next treasury review must compare the account to banking records before anyone calls this a bank reconciliation. Payroll, other accounts and historical capital funding are excluded. This limitation applies even where the arithmetic difference is zero.

documents.title: Joint board and management responsibilities
documents.text:
# Joint board and management responsibilities

Board working arrangements, confirmed July 8, 2026. Pine and River jointly appoint a six-member board: Elva Sornivet and Tovan Kelreth for Pine; Iona Varneset and Remy Delsovar for River; Sabine Morlenn and Tessa Quelvane as independent members. Sabine chairs. These are governance appointments, not ARWC employment posts.

The working quorum is four, including at least one member from each district and an independent member. Each present member has one vote; abstentions and dissent are recorded. This is the company's agreed meeting practice, not a claim about a province's legislation. A board resolution does not exercise regulatory powers.

The board considers the service plan, budgets, capital funding requests and rate proposals. Rate proposals proceed through the district owners' public consideration process; these minutes do not change any accepted tariff. Local costs belong to their receiving district. Shared-support allocation follows the agreed method, not equal ownership shares.

Elin Verrin is general manager and implements the board's direction. Luc Venn-Morel reports to Elin and is accountable for operating recommendations. Emre Edran reviews financial controls; Finn Elvarn keeps the meeting and action records. Mira Delmont coordinates reporting, obtains factual reviews and publishes only the approved public copy. Rosa Nerivet tests customer explanations, without approving accounts or speaking for the board.

Drafts, detailed reconciliations and individual learning notes have named readers. Board packs may contain restricted summary papers, but not a copy of the customer ledger. Public reports are separate releases, with their own approval and date. Public search must not expose the private pack or its draft titles.

# Completed renewal and a service people can maintain / draft P1

Mira Delmont, working draft for factual review. Not approved for publication.

The River booster project was completed in 2022.

Water service depends on ordinary renewal as well as new projects. ARWC's four selected completed projects were handed over between August 2021 and September 2023, with accepted costs totaling USD 638,880.00. These are historical project costs, not this year's cash spending.

The North reservoir inlet actuator work was handed over on August 2, 2021, at USD 181,940.00. Pine pump-hall ventilation followed on June 27, 2022, at USD 124,320.00. River booster duty-pump renewal was handed over on February 20, 2023, at USD 235,780.00. Upland telemetry-panel renewal followed on September 18, 2023, at USD 96,840.00.

The projects form part of the established staged treatment and distribution renewal history. They improved maintainability within their accepted scopes; the figures do not establish new water-source capacity. We thank the operating and engineering teams who delivered and received the work. Future renewal proposals still require their own scope, funding and acceptance.

The opening sentence is a proposed headline and needs checking against the body. Retain this version with the review comments; corrections will be made in R1.

# Learning time and the people who make it possible / draft P1

Mira Delmont, working draft for factual review. Not approved for publication.

Four completed sessions helped colleagues check ordinary work.

Four small internal sessions completed between June 18 and September 8 covered receipt allocation, board-record handover, explaining bills and comparing renewal scopes. The attendance and preparation records total 1005 person-minutes, or 16.75 person-hours. This is a bounded learning record, not every training activity across ARWC.

Participants worked through an example and checked a finished result. Attendance does not confer a new professional qualification or unrestricted authority to work alone. We thank those who taught, attended and covered ordinary work. Recognition does not require a speech or photograph. Future orientation proposals will include preparation time and continuing development, not assume that long-serving staff have chosen retirement dates. Those proposals are still to come; completing these four sessions does not settle the next group's arrangements.

The board is governing its company, not claiming provincial regulatory powers.

# Find the current invitation

documents.name: lq-specification
documents.title: ARWC Laboratory Operating Specification ARWC-LOS-26-01
documents.text:
# ARWC Laboratory Operating Specification ARWC-LOS-26-01

Effective 5 January 2026. This fictional internal specification supports routine trend review at ARWC. Its response bands are not statutory, regulatory, health, or legal limits and must not be described as such.

| Code | Working measure | Internal working band |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CRU | Clarity response, ARWC response units | 0.0 to 4.0 |
| MBU | Mineral balance, ARWC balance units | 40.0 to 75.0 |
| RSI | Reference stability, percent of laboratory reference | 92.0 to 108.0 |

Every history retains schedule, collection, receipt, analytical run, review and reporting references. A result outside an internal band is repeated or sent for recollection. It is not, by itself, a public-safety or legal conclusion.

documents.name: lq-work-guide
documents.title: Routine sample and report guide
documents.text:
# Routine sample and report guide

Use the scheduled sample identity at collection. Record the seal and receipt time before analysis. Retain preliminary and repeat runs together. A reviewer may accept a repeat, request recollection, or leave the item open. Weekly summaries state the actual disposition and never turn an open recollection into an accepted result.

The monthly workbook is a working aid. The signed review row and issued weekly report remain the authoritative history.

documents.text:
# Pine customer demand periods

Held 14 September, 09:00–09:45. Chair: Hana Radvell. Present: Nadia Corvane, Hana Radvell, Harriet Belsart, Hugo Havelin, Idris Renshaw, Imani Bravelle, Iris Iversen, Isabel Rivelin.

Papers: pl-arwc-plan-mtg-01-pack. These notes record discussion and assigned checks; no new spending or operating authority was requested.

**ARWC-PLN-26-01**
Nadia: No. Some premises have parallel supplies. Use billed volume for the daily comparator and keep the line count only as a reconciliation aid.
Recorded outcome: Use the daily billed comparator for neighbourhood information work. Request another complete quarter before estimating a trend.
Open action for Nadia Corvane, 30 September: A second quarter and an independently measured distribution input are needed before discussing seasonal growth or losses.

**ARWC-PLN-26-02**
Hana: The extract uses authoritative billed usage lines only. Internal check meters contribute no additional billed volume.
Recorded outcome: Keep master-metered buildings as a separate customer class in the demand pack. Ask Accounts for an aggregate dwelling denominator at the next refresh.
Open action for Hana Radvell, 30 September: No per-household rate is issued until the dwelling denominator is reviewed.

**ARWC-PLN-26-03**
Harriet: A single month cannot establish growth. The upper factor is a chosen sensitivity for discussion; it is not fitted to production data.
Recorded outcome: Carry June as a dated commercial comparator and ask for a second seasonal period before preparing growth assumptions.
Open action for Harriet Belsart, 30 September: Do not annualize one production month into a promised volume.

**ARWC-PLN-26-04**
Hugo: Ownership does not set consumption. Each district retains its own billed total and period; neither is adjusted to produce a 50/50 split.
Recorded outcome: Use the district total in the owner briefing and request facility opening information before developing a winter comparison.
Open action for Hugo Havelin, 30 September: A budget allocation percentage must not replace measured district consumption.

documents.name: pl-arwc-plan-method-01-method
documents.title: Planning calculations and reference boundaries
documents.text:
# Planning calculations: September comparison book

Use the dated input return, calculation file, review and issued paper together.
The input steward releases only the summary appropriate to the planning team.
Private household records do not accompany demand returns. A source count covers
the selected records at the cut-off, not everything the company has ever done.

Consumption is billed m³. Divide by the actual period days before comparing rates;
quarterly households and monthly business accounts still cover different periods.
The seasonal combination is a mixed-period reference, not simultaneous measured
demand. It does not quantify plant output, unbilled use, losses or source yield.

Renewal costs are explicit five-year undiscounted screening allowances. They are
not supplier quotations. Taxes, financing, inflation and salvage are outside the
comparison. A cheaper option still requires a suitable engineering scope.
District-specific studies belong to that district. Shared work needs the agreed
allocation at the funding stage; no automatic 50/50 split follows from ownership.

Laboratory workload distinguishes sample identities, result rows, accepted reviews
and open recollections. ARWC-LOS-26-01 is an internal operating aid,
not a legal limit. Time allowances are planning estimates, not attendance records.
August field handoffs are a narrower book than the January–July routine series.

Cairn Reach is one reserve within a wider ARWC source portfolio. Merewick's
different source exposure can support limited purchases, conditional on its own
commitments. Its ceiling is not firm available capacity. Talvern's shared Pine
facilities have a limited supplementary irrigation allowance, distinct from
household service and the growers' other sources. This book makes no reservation.

Formal approval here accepts assumptions for comparison or issues a recommendation.
Project funding, a purchase, an operational instruction and a contract acceptance
each need their own authority. Open actions stay open until a later dated record
closes them. All September 30 follow-ups remain outstanding in this book.

documents.name: rr-arwc-01-arwc
documents.title: When the familiar contact is away
documents.text:
# When the familiar contact is away

Maya Ranscombe | 23 June 2026

Theo's point was about continuity rather than a shorter response promise. A question left with one engineer should not have to be retold from the beginning when that person is away. The useful handover is the record reference, what the reviewer expected to see and the last answer already tried.

Maya will keep the customer conversation with the support history. Theo will use that conversation for a follow-up instead of opening a second personal exchange. A photograph of a local work sheet is not needed when its record reference and the disputed field will do.

This note records a working preference. It leaves ARWC's own acceptance responsibilities and the agreed support scope in place. A familiar name is welcome; an answer that survives the next shift is more useful.

documents.name: rr-arwc-02-arwc
documents.title: A useful handover question
documents.text:
# A useful handover question

Clara Morivelle | 08 July 2026

A reviewer asking whether a replacement has been accepted is asking about authority, not merely which attachment appears first. The question should name the submission being compared and the acceptance entry being read. A newer upload can still await review.

For their next technical conversation Clara and Rowan will use a written pair of descriptions, not copies of operating records. One describes a received replacement; the other describes the reviewer's later acceptance. They should remain separate sentences. Combining them into “the latest version is accepted” would make the example easier to read but wrong.

Clara will check whether the words describe ARWC's review practice. Rowan can explain the product's presentation. Neither role makes an unreviewed document effective for work.

documents.name: rr-arwc-03-arwc
documents.title: Reference conversation: questions worth asking
documents.text:
# Reference conversation: questions worth asking

Theo Marrivel | 20 August 2026

Possible questions for a future reference discussion, collected before any date or participants are agreed.

What did ARWC have to settle internally before the submission process became useful? How does a maintenance planner know which colleague still owes a review? What should a new customer budget staff time for, besides learning the screen? Theo is comfortable describing the habits that changed and the habits that did not.

The answer should include the cost of keeping local work records intelligible. It should not imply that purchasing a product makes unclear instructions disappear. There is no request here for a testimonial, slides or a public quotation. Maya will ask separately about a defined audience and staff time if the discussion develops. No customer data or operating screenshots are included.

documents.name: rr-arwc-07-arwc
documents.title: Continuity preference: a shorter question
documents.text:
# Continuity preference: a shorter question

Maya Ranscombe | 11 September 2026

The June preference was to keep the last answer with the original customer question. Theo has now clarified the smallest useful follow-up: state what remains unclear, quote the disputed label and preserve the existing reference. Resending an entire handover pack makes the recipient guess which part has changed.

Maya's reply should identify the next person responsible if the question needs a different role. “Passed on” alone leaves Theo unable to tell whether he should wait or supply more information. This is an expectation about useful communication, not a new response-time commitment.

Theo does not want weekly status mail when there is no open question. An answer should close its own small loop. If a later shift has a different question, it can say what has changed rather than repeat the original request.

documents.name: rr-arwc-08
documents.title: ARWC reference: private preparation reminder
documents.text:
# ARWC reference: private preparation reminder

Clara Morivelle | 14 September 2026

Clara's preparation reminder for Theo: talk about the review process we use, including the parts we still perform ourselves. Keep local plant and staff detail out of the example. A prospective customer needs to hear what a reviewer does, not learn our asset naming scheme.

Theo can describe planning and handover habits. Clara can explain why receipt and acceptance are separate. Neither needs to represent every department or describe a colleague's support question. If a question falls outside their experience, they can leave it for the appropriate owner.

The September 29 hold is still a hold. This is a private reminder for the two invited ARWC colleagues, not approved minutes, a statement on behalf of management or permission to publish their comments. No further staff time has been agreed here.

documents.name: rr-arwc-10-arwc
documents.title: Reference hold: morning status
documents.text:
# Reference hold: morning status

Maya Ranscombe | 16 September 2026

Status at 07:45 on 16 September: the proposed ARWC reference conversation remains on 29 September, 10:00–10:30, with prospective participants unconfirmed. The agreed agenda and sixty ARWC person-minutes remain the preparation basis. No slides, public quotation or recording permission has been added.

Theo and Clara will discuss their own experience of maintenance submissions and review. Martin still owes the participant confirmation. If the audience or time changes, he must bring that change back to the invited colleagues rather than silently treating the current hold as general availability.

This is a preparation status note, not a second invitation. The existing calendar occurrence remains authoritative. There has been no call, attendance, completion or customer endorsement to report.

documents.name: rr-veybridge-01
documents.title: Visit feedback / ARWC-PO-26-201
documents.text:
# Visit feedback / ARWC-PO-26-201

Theo Marrivel | 18 June 2026

VB-SR-26-001 records the standard commissioning witness visit on 12 June, 13:00–16:00, against ARWC-WO-26-0181. ARWC-GR-26-001 records receipt on 15 June. The accepted order amount is USD 1,240.00; this follow-up does not add work to it.

Theo found the report reference easier to use than the diary subject when answering the next planner. Jules asks that later questions keep both the order and report numbers. A visit date alone can refer to several jobs in his diary.

For a subsequent booking, dispatch should receive the scheduling question. Jules remains the useful contact for an observation he actually made. There is no request for a return visit in this feedback, and no finding that the accepted service needs repeating.

documents.name: rr-veybridge-02
documents.title: Dispatch desk / a booking request that can be used
documents.text:
# Dispatch desk / a booking request that can be used

Dana Veskell | 30 June 2026

Dana's dispatch note for ARWC: begin with the order reference, the requested attendance window and the person who can settle access arrangements. Say whether the time is a request or an already agreed appointment. A forwarded chain with “same as last time” does not tell dispatch which details still apply.

Dana can coordinate the diary without asking Jules to relay each message from the road. A change to scope or travel still needs written authority through the purchasing route. Dispatch cannot infer that authority from a friendly request to stay longer.

For uncertain dates, give the constraint that matters: a planner being available is different from the site being ready. Dana will return one clear question if the booking lacks that information, rather than copy every earlier contact into a new thread.

documents.name: rr-veybridge-03
documents.title: Report question / the last line
documents.text:
# Report question / the last line

Jules Orswick | 02 July 2026

Review of VB-SR-26-006, the 26 June visit against ARWC-PO-26-206 and ARWC-WO-26-0271. The report records serviceable condition for the stated scope. Its result does not extend to equipment outside that order.

Jules would like later questions to point to an observation or a missing explanation. “Can you sign the whole thing off?” is too broad: he can stand behind the observations he made, while ARWC's reviewer owns its acceptance decision. The report and receipt remain separate records.

Theo will retain the report with the accepted job and use its reference when asking a specific question. This writing feedback leaves the original report intact. It records no additional inspection, revisited condition or new engineering conclusion.

documents.name: rr-veybridge-04
documents.title: Account desk / summer service review
documents.text:
# Account desk / summer service review

Aiden Rellard | 22 July 2026

Aiden's service-review note concerns the standard visit arrangement, not a new service package. Under A-S-001-AGR-01 a standard visit is USD 1,240. Travel or extra scope needs a written order. A diary confirmation cannot supply that order.

Priya wants future quotations to make additional attendance conspicuous rather than bury it in a description of the standard service. Aiden can keep the standard visit and a separately requested addition on separate lines. That makes a decision easier without assuming the addition will be bought.

There is no blanket instruction to add travel to accepted summer jobs. Their existing quotations, reports, receipts and payment records stand. The account desk will use this preference when an actual new request arrives; it does not create a purchase by itself.

documents.name: rr-veybridge-05
documents.title: Visit feedback / a different familiar face

# Visit feedback / a different familiar face

Theo Marrivel | 28 July 2026

ARWC's note after VB-SR-26-012 and ARWC-GR-26-012. The 14 July appointment was delivered under ARWC-PO-26-212, for the accepted USD 1,240.00 standard visit. The report is the evidence of service, regardless of which familiar contact arranged the diary.

The next booking still needs its own accepted order and appointment. This feedback is about continuity after completed work. It is neither a standing booking nor a promise that the same specialist will attend every future job.

documents.name: rr-veybridge-06
documents.title: Teaching notes / describing an observation
documents.text:
# Teaching notes / describing an observation

Jules Orswick | 06 August 2026

Jules is collecting a small teaching example for newer field colleagues. The invented note says “checked, all fine”. The exercise is to ask what was checked, under which order and what the person actually observed. There is deliberately no real plant, reading or acceptance signature to borrow.

A useful answer does not have to become an essay. It should let the next person distinguish a direct observation from something reported by somebody else. If the writer did not see the result, they should say who supplied it rather than adopt it as their own inspection.

Theo can comment on what makes a report usable for planning. Veybridge owns its own training decisions and staff competence. Sharing this wording example does not qualify anybody, book an ARWC training session or change the scope of a field visit.

documents.name: rr-veybridge-07
documents.title: Dispatch feedback / one changed detail
documents.text:
# Dispatch feedback / one changed detail

Dana Veskell | 18 August 2026

A follow-up to the June dispatch note. When changing a proposed time, keep the original order reference and state the changed detail at the start. Sending a fresh subject without the reference makes it look like another visit request. Keeping an obsolete time buried above the change makes the other error possible.

Dana's preferred reply is a compact confirmation of the new proposal and the remaining question. It should not silently carry forward a site-access name that has not been checked. Theo will say when only the planner's availability has changed.

No actual appointment is moved by this note. Existing accepted appointment records remain the source for their dates. The account team will revisit the wording if a real booking shows a difficulty; there is no need for a recurring reminder when nothing has changed.

documents.name: rr-veybridge-08
documents.title: Practical workshop / return information
documents.text:
# Practical workshop / return information

Jules Orswick | 03 September 2026

Jules's response to Ardenvale's autumn workshop question. A return example is useful if it shows the information that lets the service desk identify the item and understand the reported problem. It should also show what is still unknown. A copied diagnosis from another job would make the example look complete for the wrong reason.

Clara has asked for the practical session to be separate from the product demonstration. Jules supports that arrangement: a field colleague should be able to attend for the work question without staying for a catalogue tour. No date or place has been selected.

Ardenvale may use this feedback to shape its programme. It does not receive Veybridge customer records or ARWC instrument histories through this exchange. Any practical handling instruction must come from the appropriate service information for the actual item.

documents.name: rr-veybridge-09

documents.text:
# Internal note / specialist continuity

Theo Marrivel | 08 September 2026

Theo's internal account note: the summer reports are usable and the dispatch replies are helping the relationship depend less on one specialist's phone. Keep that distinction in the next supplier review. We can value Jules's practical judgment without routing every booking through him.

Priya should ask about the supplier's route for continuity, not request a guarantee of one named person for all visits. If an actual future job needs particular experience, explain that in its scope before ordering. A preference expressed in a friendly conversation is not an accepted personnel condition.

Jules's interest in teaching is his own development at Veybridge. ARWC has not offered him employment, appointed him as an internal trainer or acquired authority to allocate his time. This note stays with the two ARWC account colleagues.

Reece's draft teaching note distinguishes identifying information from a diagnosis. The service desk needs the item's own reference, the reported behavior, when it was noticed and a contact who can explain the circumstances. If a detail is unknown, write that rather than borrowing it from an earlier return.

A photograph can help identify a label when suitable to share, but it should not bring unrelated work papers or people into the picture. The example for discussion will use an invented label. No actual instrument is being shipped under this note.

Physical preparation, permitted packaging and any handling restrictions must be checked against the item's service instructions. This page is about the information accompanying a return. It is not generic permission to pack or send any item in the same way.

No replacement parts were included in this completed service. A discussion of possible equipment later must have its own question and quotation. Return example: an incomplete note that can be answered

The desk response should ask for the observation time and the person who has the sheet, then check the relevant service route. It should not turn “display changed” into an assumed failure mode. The useful lesson is that a limited observation can still be passed on honestly.

Clara suggests leaving the unknown time visible in the first version, then adding it in a later exercise step. The teaching version has no actual serial number, operating site, personal data or customer attachment. It is suitable for a written discussion while the autumn session dates remain open.

The account desk has recorded ARWC's preference for clearer headings. A request for advice on a return is not an order to repair. A repair quotation is not authority to supply a replacement. Using those words interchangeably creates unnecessary purchasing questions.

Vera will identify which decision a future quotation is asking the customer to make. If parts are an option, they should appear as an option with their own price rather than inside a description of a completed service. Priya still owns ARWC's written purchasing response.

Reece will keep the exercise separate from item-specific handling instructions. documents.text:
# Forecast return: information before a request

Gideon Sarrick | 04 August 2026

Gideon's requested forecast description should state the period, the customer's estimate and the assumptions that would change it. It should distinguish a planning range from a quantity the customer is asking to reserve. A blank return cannot be read as zero demand, and a forecast cannot be read as an accepted order.

Nadia will identify which parts of an ARWC estimate are measured history and which are assumptions. She does not need to send customer-level account data to explain a regional planning range. If the estimate changes, the later version should name the earlier date and the reason.

Merewick has its own maintenance and member planning to consider. Receiving better information helps that work; it does not make uncommitted capacity certain. No new quantity, reservation or delivery is agreed by this note.

documents.name: rr-merewick-05
documents.title: Account distinction: customer and member returns
documents.text:
# Account distinction: customer and member returns

Mabel Dornell | 12 August 2026

ARWC is an external contract customer of Merewick, not a member owner. Its account correspondence belongs under A-S-003. A member planning meeting and a customer request can concern similar information without conferring the same standing.

Mabel will send ARWC the customer-facing information request when relevant. She will not forward another member's return or a member-only discussion to explain an available date. Priya can supply the particulars of ARWC's request and ask whether they are sufficient for an account response.

The agreement remains a limited supplementary-supply arrangement, with availability confirmed per request. This note changes no rights, voting role or ownership interest. It also does not make ARWC responsible for predicting the cooperative's wider commitments. Each party can explain its own planning constraints without disclosing somebody else's confidential return.

documents.name: rr-merewick-06
documents.title: Planning note: ceiling is not firm supply
documents.text:
# Planning note: ceiling is not firm supply

Nadia Corvane | 24 August 2026

Nadia's internal reminder uses the three accepted Merewick activities: 2,250 m³, with accepted charges of USD 2,070.00. Subtracting the quantity from the 20,000 m³ annual ceiling gives 17,750 m³. It does not establish physical availability or a right to call on that quantity at any chosen time.

A forecast can carry the agreement as context while keeping unconfirmed supply outside a firm total. A later request needs a dated response and accepted reservation. The current record supplies neither for a new delivery.

Priya should remain the account route for commercial availability questions. Nadia can explain the planning assumptions without presenting them as purchasing authority. This note stays with ARWC's two responsible colleagues; it is not a supplier commitment and should not be forwarded as one.

documents.name: rr-merewick-07
documents.title: Forecast version note: what changed
documents.text:
# Forecast version note: what changed

Gideon Sarrick | 03 September 2026

A revised forecast should identify the earlier return by date, retain the same period and say which assumption changed. Replacing the attachment without explanation forces the recipient to compare numbers without knowing why they differ. If the period changes as well, say so at the start.

Gideon and Nadia discussed using a short version note with the return. The example is descriptive: “The planning range has changed because the assumed timing changed; this is still a forecast.” It carries no invented quantity and is not a request for a reservation.

The earlier return should remain available to the people who used it. A later estimate does not retrospectively alter an accepted delivery. This working note gives the two planners a consistent question to ask when a revision arrives, without sharing member or individual customer information.

documents.name: rr-merewick-08

documents.text:
# Customer information request: minimum useful fields

Mabel Dornell | 07 September 2026

The account desk's information checklist asks for ARWC's account reference, the period being discussed, the quantity and units if a quantity is proposed, and whether the note is a forecast or an actual request. It also needs a contact who can answer a follow-up before any offer expires.

If the question is about an existing delivery, use its accepted reference instead. The desk should not turn a historical reconciliation into a request for another delivery. Nor should an incomplete planning note silently become an order because it contains a number.

Priya has asked for the distinction to appear near the start of future correspondence. Mabel agrees. This checklist is not an offer form carrying reserved capacity. The per-request availability and acceptance process remains necessary under A-S-003-AGR-01.

# A-B-001 / reading explanation retained

Rosa Nerivet | 27 July 2026

Account note for Lila, following ARWC-BC-2026-0001. Invoice ARWC-INV-2026-048481 uses actual readings 210631 and 218731 on meter ARWC-M-048751. The difference is 8,100 m³. The reading question was explained on 23 July; this note retains the explanation for the accounts file.

| 210631 | Earlier actual reading used on the usage line |
| 218731 | Later actual reading used on the usage line |

The total is the metered interval quantity. It does not say which production run used the water. Lila can use the bill reference to ask a further account question without reopening the answered reading query as a new complaint.

documents.name: rr-belvarn-02
documents.title: Production notebook: three dates on a water bill
documents.text:
# Production notebook: three dates on a water bill

Bram Vellard | 03 August 2026

Bram's question sheet for the production team.

Bill issue date: when the bill was issued. Reading dates: the dates of the readings used for the consumption calculation. Production dates: our own dates for making particular orders. These can describe different intervals and should not be put in the same column just because a spreadsheet wants one date.

Before comparing water use with output, identify the interval each number covers and the unit used. If the periods do not line up, mark the comparison as incomplete. A precise division of mismatched totals is still a poor comparison.

Rosa can explain the account entries. Belvarn must supply its own production information and decide how to compare it. This notebook does not claim a saving, assign consumption to a particular line or propose a meter change.

documents.name: rr-belvarn-03
documents.title: Appointment request card: ask the production office
documents.text:
# Appointment request card: ask the production office

Bram Vellard | 11 August 2026

Belvarn's practical contact card for arranging a meter appointment at the River plant.

Use the production office to establish a current workable window. The mix of short runs means that a convenient time in one week may be poor in the next. Ask for the named person meeting the visitor and the access point when the actual appointment is being arranged.

Do not infer an appointment from a question about a bill. Do not carry a suggested time forward indefinitely. Once the appointment team and Belvarn agree the time, retain that confirmation where the staff on duty can find it.

This card supplies the contact preference only. There is no new visit date, completed meter work or change to the water account. The agreed appointment record for any actual work will carry those details.

documents.name: rr-belvarn-04
documents.title: Short-run planning: what advance notice helps
documents.text:
# Short-run planning: what advance notice helps

Bram Vellard | 24 August 2026

Bram's feedback about planned-visit communication is practical: name the purpose, proposed window and person who needs to respond. “An engineer may attend” leaves production unable to judge whether the proposal touches a busy part of the day.

An early proposal can still be useful if it says what remains unsettled. Bram would rather see a provisional window clearly described than a confident date copied from an internal diary before anyone has asked the plant. The final confirmation must then distinguish itself from the proposal.

The smaller runs are a business scheduling concern, not evidence of a water-service incident. Belvarn has not reported a supply interruption in this exchange. Rosa will retain the communication preference and ask the appointment team to use it when there is an actual request.

documents.name: rr-belvarn-05
documents.title: Careers conversation: questions before an invitation
documents.text:
# Careers conversation: questions before an invitation

Lila Perrow | 02 September 2026

Belvarn maintains an apprenticeship relationship with its local training college. Lila is collecting possible subjects for a later careers conversation: how an experienced employee explains a routine task, how a new colleague knows when to ask for help, and what makes a useful handover.

The idea is not yet an event invitation. There is no date, speaker list or commitment of ARWC staff time. Rosa has asked for the intended audience and format before suggesting whether a colleague could contribute. A discussion of everyday work may suit; a technical demonstration would be a different request.

Lila will take the questions back to the people planning the conversation. Belvarn's interest in apprenticeships belongs to its own business life. It is not a condition attached to its water account or a promised customer benefit.

documents.name: rr-belvarn-06
documents.title: Efficiency enquiry: information needed before a comparison
documents.text:
# Efficiency enquiry: information needed before a comparison

Rosa Nerivet | 09 September 2026

The production office is considering an efficiency project. The first account question is what the ordinary meter bill can and cannot tell the team. Its readings describe consumption over the identified interval; they do not allocate that consumption to particular products or short runs.

A useful comparison needs matching periods and a stated production measure. Belvarn should also decide what operational changes occurred during the period before attributing a difference to an efficiency measure. Rosa can explain the bill entries, but does not have the plant's internal production records.

The billing-period explanation is being finalized separately and will be sent when ready. This enquiry has no promised saving, equipment recommendation, appointment or changed tariff. Bram will first identify the internal question the comparison is supposed to answer.

documents.name: rr-belvarn-07

documents.text:
# Working comparison card for the production desk

Bram Vellard | 10 September 2026

Bram's working comparison card after the account explanation:

| Question | Information to put beside it |
| --- | --- |
| Which interval? | Start and end of both the metered and production records |
| Which quantity? | Metered m³ and the chosen production measure, separately labeled |
| What changed? | Known changes in run mix or working pattern during that interval |
| What is missing? | Unmatched periods or incomplete production information |

The card has no efficiency result because Belvarn has not supplied a matching production series in this conversation. Rosa has checked only that the bill side is described as an interval quantity. The next internal task is to decide which records Belvarn wants to compare. A blank result is preferable to an unsupported savings claim.

The July reading query is already explained. The September efficiency enquiry asks how to use the bill information; it is not a reported supply problem. Rosa has promised the finished billing-period explanation when ready, not a free assessment of the plant's efficiency proposal.

For Belvarn's efficiency discussion, use it to establish which interval a bill describes before comparing that bill with production information. It does not supply production data or attribute consumption to individual runs. A specific reading question can still be answered against the named bill.

# Account follow-up: questions retained, visit unbooked

Member Services circular file

Member questions: which arrangement are we discussing?

Nico Pelwick · 05 August 2026

Nico's question card for a later information session.

Does the supplementary allowance describe all the water a member uses? No; it concerns the shared Pine facilities under the stated contract. Can a household bill be answered from the cooperative total? No; the relevant household account has its own information. Is the seasonal maximum a record of actual delivery? No; delivered quantities need their dated accepted references.

A useful first question from the presenter is “Which arrangement do you mean?” It is less intimidating than asking a member to know the right department before speaking. A personal account question should then move to the appropriate private route rather than be answered in front of the group.

The card contains proposed explanations only. There is no new session date or completed attendance record.

“Our ARWC arrangement is a limited supplementary supply for the shared Pine facilities. The seasonal maximum is 7,500 m³ during June–September. Actual supplied quantities are recorded against accepted deliveries. This arrangement does not replace each member's other water arrangements.”

Priya has been asked to check that description of the contract. Talvern will decide the notice's audience and publication route. The draft does not set internal member charges, promise equal shares or convert the ceiling into available water.

Selma prefers a short explanatory paragraph with the member-services contact beside it. A long list of exceptions would obscure the first distinction people need. Questions about another arrangement should be directed to the right account owner rather than answered from this paragraph.

Nico's scheduling note explains why Talvern cannot simply add another subject to the next member meeting. The packing and storage discussion already needs time for members to compare a staged approach with one larger interruption. Different members have different busy periods and will not all find the same week convenient.

The water-information session should have its own useful time rather than become the last item after a long debate. A written question list can be collected while the dates are reconsidered. Members who cannot attend should still have a route to the general explanation.

There is no agreed facility investment or construction programme in this note. ARWC is not being asked to decide the cooperative's packing project. Rosa needs the scheduling constraint so she can offer a suitable information arrangement later.

documents.title: Description workshop note / identify, then interpret
documents.text:
TERNWICK / ARWC RECORDS CORRESPONDENCE
Description workshop note / identify, then interpret
Filed 25 August 2026; Huw Delvern

Worked wording example, not a description of an actual photograph:

Starting description: “Old office.” Reader question: which office, and what in the available record supports that identification? Better working description: “Office interior; location not established in the accompanying note.” If an authoritative label is later found, record that source before making the location definite.

Huw prefers a candid uncertainty to a confident guess. Dario wants readers to find the item even while that question remains open, so the stable reference should accompany the description. Searchable wording and settled historical identification are related tasks, not the same task.

This example teaches a description habit. It adds no facts to an accepted ARWC image, names no unidentified person and does not alter any completed batch's acceptance or amount.

documents.name: rr-ternwick-07

documents.text:
TERNWICK / ARWC RECORDS CORRESPONDENCE
Records desk: selection before a proposal
Filed 09 September 2026; Dario Torren

Dario's internal note for the next possible Ternwick request. Start by identifying which records need additional description and what a reader cannot currently determine. “Make the archive easier to use” is a reasonable ambition but too broad to price as a task.

A selection list should preserve the current item reference, the present description and the question to resolve. Where there is no evidence for an identification, the task may be to record uncertainty more clearly rather than discover a definite answer. The supplier should not be asked to guess names or locations to fill a column.

Priya can seek a proposal after the selection and desired output are settled. No new batch, price, purchase order or completion date is authorized here. The accepted histories and their returned originals remain unchanged.

documents.name: rr-ternwick-08
documents.title: Proposal preparation card / description work
documents.text:
TERNWICK / ARWC RECORDS CORRESPONDENCE
Proposal preparation card / description work
Filed 10 September 2026; Edie Ransell

Edie's preparation card for a possible description proposal:

Item reference — keep the existing reference. Present description — supply the text the reader sees now. Question — explain what the reader cannot tell. Available evidence — identify the label, note or other material that might answer it. Desired output — say whether ARWC wants a corrected description, a recorded uncertainty or a cross-reference.

A proposal can then distinguish the selected work from a new scanning batch. Returning a description question does not itself place an order, and the current batch price cannot be assumed to include an open-ended research task.

Dario will complete the selection at ARWC before requesting a price. Edie can comment on whether the stated output is clear. The card contains no actual unapproved selection or invented historical identification.

It should end with a clearer request, not an assumption that every interesting archive question has become contracted work. If the selection is still too uncertain, a written exchange may be enough.

This is a future appointment proposal. It has no attendance, minutes or completed description work. The accepted scanning batches and their amounts remain as recorded. Any later order requires the normal purchasing decision.

documents.name: service-register-guide
documents.title: Customer Accounts: opening register and joins
documents.text:
# Customer Accounts: opening register and joins

Owner: Customer Accounts. Revision 1, September 15, 2026.

The opening financial position is July 1, 2026, at 18:00 (UTC−04:00). Contact and
preference views include accepted changes through September 15. Opening balances
remain historical: do not replace them with later receipts or contact changes.
This is the opening register and its account-service history, not the complete
July–September billing run. The only later financial entries included here are
Talvern's two already-settled July deliveries, retained with their delivery references.

An account is a payer relationship. A customer is its named holder; the account
contact is the person authorized to correspond. A service point is a physical
water connection. A meter measures a supply or checks part of it. None of those
is a count of residents. Customers do not acquire staff or plant access by
appearing in this register.

Use account_id to join accounts, contacts, preferences, account-services,
invoices, receipts, opening-balances, changes and cases. Use service_point_id
for service points, relationships, meters and invoice lines. Meter readings join
on meter_id; usage lines identify their exact start and end reading IDs. Tariff
and period IDs identify the effective version and the interval, never a display
label. IDs remain stable after a postal or display-name correction.

Each customer in this opening register has one billing account. Some accounts
serve multiple points. Relationships have inclusive start and exclusive end
dates; a blank end is current. A contact preference does not transfer liability.
Display corrections preserve the customer ID. Account closure, new occupiers,
physical disconnection and changes of service responsibility require their own
records; none should be inferred from these preference cases.

Population estimates count occupied dwellings at service points. They are
planning counts, not named resident records. Pine: 33,750 dwellings and 90,000
residents. River: 26,250 dwellings and 70,000 residents. Each district's homes
include houses and 25-dwelling apartment buildings. A building owner receives
the master bill; the utility does not also bill those apartments individually.

Field colleagues receive service points, meters and readings. The customer
register, balances and correspondence stay with authorized Customer Accounts
staff. Procurement sees the relevant commercial agreement, not the residential
contact register. A statement may be given to its verified account contact;
whole register exports must never be attached to a customer message.

A blank phone field means no number is retained in this view. Do not manufacture
one or treat email permission as consent for a different channel. A one-off
opening-statement email is distinct from recurring bill-delivery consent.

documents.name: service-tariff-guide
documents.title: Water charges: 2026 tariff and cadence
documents.text:
# Water charges: 2026 tariff and cadence

Rate authority: ARWC-RATES-2026-01, effective January 1–December 31, 2026.
Reference retained: ARWC-RATES-2025-01. The listed 2025 and 2026 rates are unchanged;
the annual version IDs identify the authority applying to a consumption period.
Rates apply equally in Pine and River. Currency is USD. These water tariffs have
zero tax and contain no wastewater charge. Wastewater remains a separate municipal
service. These are the approved ARWC charges, not a general tax or legal guide.

| Class | Fixed charge | Measured water | Cadence |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| HOME | USD 24.00 per service point | USD 1.40/m³ | Calendar quarter |
| MASTER | USD 24.00 per occupied dwelling | USD 1.40/m³ | Calendar quarter |
| BUSINESS | USD 18.00 per service point | USD 1.65/m³ | Calendar month |
| MUNICIPAL | USD 18.00 per service point | USD 1.65/m³ | Calendar month |
| SEASONAL | None | USD 1.15/m³ | Accepted delivery |

Quarterly and monthly invoices are dated the first day after the period and are
due 20 days later. Period end is exclusive: the reading at that boundary closes
the old period and may open the next. Do not create an invoice merely because a
future billing-period row exists. The opening residential period is ARWC-2026-Q2;
business and municipal opening periods are ARWC-2026-M06. ARWC-2026-Q3 and
ARWC-2026-M09 remain open at the September 16 snapshot.

Usage is the accepted end register minus the accepted start register, multiplied
by the meter multiplier. Registers and invoiced volumes are in m³. Each fixed
or usage line is rounded half up to two decimal places; sum the rounded lines
for the invoice. No estimated readings or rollover are present in the opening
interval. Both parallel feeds count; a downstream private check meter does not.
Meter exchanges contribute two non-overlapping intervals and one fixed charge
for the service point. Replacement meters start at zero, not the removed value.

The opening dataset includes paid, part-paid, unpaid and credit accounts. A
receipt and an allocation are different records. The amount allocated may not
exceed the receipt or invoice. Credit stays unapplied until a later allocation
or authorized refund; a negative balance is not an extra charge. No late charge,
interest, deposit, tax or unexplained balance-forward is part of this opening.

Talvern has a separate discretionary allowance, ARWC-W-SEASONAL-2026-v1,
under A-B-002-AGR-01: up to 7,500 m³ each June–September season, only for shared
Pine facilities. It is billed per accepted delivery, due 14 days after delivery.
The accepted June 12 delivery is 450 m³ (USD 517.50); July 2 is 620 m³
(USD 713.00); July 20 is 500 m³ (USD 575.00). All three are settled. Season-to-date
use is 1,570 m³, leaving an allowance ceiling of 5,930 m³, subject to availability.
That ceiling is not a reservation or a promise of further supply.

documents.name: service-meter-guide
documents.title: Meter relationships and opening reads
documents.text:
# Meter relationships and opening reads

Owner: Meter services. September 15, 2026.

There are 50,460 active water service points. The 51,210 active meters comprise
51,060 supply meters used for billing and 150 private check meters. The register
also retains 120 removed supply meters. Its 51,330 meter records are devices,
not service points or customers.

The 600 premises with parallel supply feeds have two billable meters. Add those
volumes once, but charge one fixed service-point amount. At 150 apartment
buildings the downstream check meter has parent_meter_id pointing at the supply
meter. Its owner is the building owner; exclude it from every invoice. A master
building's fixed tariff uses its 25 occupied dwellings, not its device count.

The 120 exchanges run from May 4 through June 12, four planned exchanges per
weekday. Each retains the old removal reading and the new installation reading
at the same instant (UTC−04:00). The old interval is closed there;
the new interval begins there. predecessor_id links the devices; supply_path
stays constant. Serial numbers never move from one physical device to another.
The historical installation read predates the opening interval; it is not a
second billable start reading for that period.

The early device installation records do not claim that the current account
holder occupied the site at installation. Service infrastructure can predate
the payer relationship. The opening consumption interval falls inside the
current account's service responsibility in every case.

Talvern's supply register records each accepted delivery cumulatively. Its
July 1 opening read equals the settled June 12 read because there was no
intervening delivery. July 2 and July 20 advance that same register. Do not
invoice the July 1 observation in addition to the accepted delivery intervals.

Period-boundary actual readings are scheduled remote register snapshots, not
simultaneous visits by a field crew. Installation and exchange readings are
recorded on site. A register timestamp does not imply continuous plant access.

These retail meters measure supplied water. They are not reservoir process
tags, engineering calibration records, or allocation-model exports. Route IDs
organize meter-service work; they do not confer control-system authority.

documents.name: service-contact-guide
documents.title: Contact changes and copies
documents.text:
# Contact changes and copies

Customer Accounts, September 15, 2026.

Ask what should change before saving a preference. A one-off paper copy, recurring
paper bills and routine service letters are three different requests. A postal
routing note does not move a water connection. A name-spacing correction does
not add a new person or transfer responsibility.

Use the verified account contact. Record the clarification, the customer's
answer, the field before and after, and the effective time. Never request a
bank statement or full bank details to find a payment: the dated receipt
reference is enough for these opening-account checks.

A routine contact window is a preference, not an appointment. Urgent service
information is not held until the preferred window. Large print has no charge.
A paper-copy queue entry means queued; it does not prove dispatch or delivery.
The retained ten copy requests are still queued in these case records.

For a meter-label question, distinguish the supply meter from a private check
meter. For a second site, confirm whether responsibility changed before
explaining the combined bill. An account explanation must not silently amend a
reading, add a charge or move a service point between districts.
